#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {

Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"

  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;

  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"

  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

```js
var DEFAULT_PARK_LABEL = 'provider_quota';
var DEFAULT_PROBE_EVERY_TICKS = 3;

function classifyFailure(text) → {
  kind: 'quota_exhausted' | 'transient' | null,
  provider: string|null,
  window: string|null,  // quota window text e.g. "weekly (7-day)"
  evidence: string|null // short matched evidence line
}

function parkLabelOf(jobParams)
function probeEveryOf(jobParams)
function probeCommandOf(jobParams) // default fa-provider ping via curl
function parkComment(classification, parkLabel)
function probeDue(probeCount, everyN) // probeCount = number of probe markers already posted
function probeMarkerLine(n) // 'quota-probe: <n>'
function countProbeMarkers(bodies) 
```

Classification regexes:
- QUOTA_PATTERNS (each → evidence):
 - /403[\s\S]{0,200}?(usage.limit|quota|billing|insufficient|credits?)/i — 403 with usage-limit body
 - /(usage.limit|quota|billing)[\s\S]{0,120}?403/i
 - /(weekly|daily|monthly|hourly)\s*(\([^)]*\))?\s*(usage\s*)?limit/i — window text capture
 - /provider chain exhausted/i — only when quota evidence also present? UT-1 says: mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted. "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses. If text has "Provider chain exhausted" AND (403 or usage-limit) → quota. If "Provider chain exhausted" alone without any quota/403/429 signals → hmm, ambiguous. Live message: "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2" appeared after 403s; the tail message alone might not include the 403s. The classifier receives the full CLI output text (developmentSummary/cliErrorMessage) — in live case the full text had the 403s. I'll treat "provider chain exhausted" + any quota-ish term (usage limit, quota) anywhere in the text → quota_exhausted; "provider chain exhausted" alone → transient? Safer: alone → null (unknown) → falls to existing behavior (reset, i.e., today's behavior). But UT-1 only requires: 403-weekly → quota; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota. Keep "exhausted"-alone → null.
- 429 / rate limit / timeout / ECONNRESET / ETIMEDOUT / "interupted" → transient (lower priority than quota).

Provider extraction:
- /([a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9.-]*[a-z0-9])?\.(?:ai|com|org|net|dev))\s+([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)\s+(?:answered|returned|responded with)\s+403/ → provider = domain
- /provider[:\s"']+([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/i fallback
- /([\w.-]+)\/[\w.-]+ answered 403/? Keep simple.

Window extraction:
- /((?:weekly|daily|monthly|hourly)(?:\s*\([^)]*\))?)\s+(?:usage\s+)?limit/i
- /(7-day|24-hour|30-day)\s+(?:usage\s+)?limit/i
Return first match text.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

For the `validation_failed` case, the githubSource.js has sticky park logic. For Jira tickets, the skipIfLabel mechanism is per-rule config. The ticket's AC2 says: "The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes" — meaning dev rules (story_development, bug_development) should skip tickets labeled `provider_quota`.

Options:
1. Add the park label to the skipIfLabels of dispatch rules in sm.json. But skipIfLabel is per-rule; the story_development rule has `skipIfLabel: sm_story_development_triggered`. Adding `provider_quota` there would skip parking. But sm.json is the base config and project repos can override. That's config — acceptable.
2. Or handle in smAgent.js: filter out candidates with the park label before dispatch.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"

  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"

  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;

  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"

  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

The fa agent exited 1 — likely no outputs/response.md, so the reset path is recoverNoChangesOutcome Case B (no git changes AND no response.md) or ensureResponseForPrBody (response.md missing after commit).

- add label `provider_quota` to ticket (and PR if present)

Plan:

1. **New module** `js/common/quotaCircuitBreaker.js` (pure logic, GralJS-compatible: `var`, plain functions, no template literals):
  - `classifyFailure(texts...)` → `{ kind: 'quota_exhausted'|'transient'|null, provider, window, resetCondition }`
    - quota signals: /HTTP 403/ + /(usage limit|quota|billing|insufficient)/i; "weekly (7-day) usage limit"; "Provider chain exhausted" with quota context.
    - transient signals: 429, timeout, ECONNRESET, "rate limit" with 429.
    - Priority: if quota signals present → quota_exhausted; else if transient signals → transient; else null.
    - Extract provider name (e.g. "z.ai", provider ids), quota window text ("weekly (7-day)"), reset condition.
  - `parkLabelOf(jobParams)` → jobParams.quotaParkLabel || 'provider_quota'
  - `probeCadenceOf(jobParams)` → jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks || 3
  - `shouldProbe(ticket, tickIndex)` — decide probe eligibility per cadence; based on a stored probe-count marker or label age. Simpler: store a `provider_quota_probe_<n>` comment/marker? Or use Jira label with counter? The AC: "one cheap provider ping per N ticks". Implementation: the SM rule for probing runs every tick (localExecution), the handler counts ticks since last probe via a marker comment on the ticket (e.g. a hidden marker line), and only probes when count % N == 0.

2. **Hook into developTicketAndCreatePR.js** (and developBugAndCreatePR.js): in `resetInterruptedDevelopment`, before posting/reseting, classify from `ctx.cliErrorMessage` / `ctx.developmentSummary`. If quota_exhausted → `parkForQuota(ctx, classification)`:
  - add label to ticket via getTracker().addLabel(ticketKey, label)
  - add label to PR if present (ctx may have prNumber? In the interrupted path, likely no PR yet — "and the PR if present")
  - post comment naming provider, quota window, reset condition
  - remove WIP label
  - do NOT move to Ready For Development
  - throw marked error err.quotaPark = true so run is RED; add to rethrownAsIs.
   
  For the probe to have a chance to un-park, the ticket stays in its current status (In Development or wherever) but the park label excludes it from SM dispatch lanes.

3. **SM exclusion**: in smAgent.js, skip dispatch candidates carrying the park label. Look at candidate filtering near line 1301/1491 — that's for skipIfLabel. But base rules in sm.json — better to handle centrally: if ticket has `provider_quota` label (configurable via jobParams), skip dispatch for ALL rules except the probe rule. Let me look at the filtering code.

4. **Probe rule**: new agent config `quota_quota_probe.json` (root JSON, JSRunner style Teammate with skipAIProcessing) + `js/quotaParkProbe.js`:
  - JQL: tickets with the park label (label = provider_quota)

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

### 1. New module `js/common/quotaCircuitBreaker.js` (pure, no globals)

```js
var DEFAULT_PARK_LABEL = 'provider_quota';
var DEFAULT_PROBE_EVERY_TICKS = 3;

function classifyFailure(text) → {
  kind: 'quota_exhausted' | 'transient' | null,
  provider: string|null,
  window: string|null,  // quota window text e.g. "weekly (7-day)"
  evidence: string|null // short matched evidence line
}

function parkLabelOf(jobParams)
function probeEveryOf(jobParams)
function probeCommandOf(jobParams) // default fa-provider ping via curl
function parkComment(classification, parkLabel)
function probeDue(probeCount, everyN) // probeCount = number of probe markers already posted
function probeMarkerLine(n) // 'quota-probe: <n>'
function countProbeMarkers(bodies) 
```

Classification regexes:
- QUOTA_PATTERNS (each → evidence):
 - /403[\s\S]{0,200}?(usage.limit|quota|billing|insufficient|credits?)/i — 403 with usage-limit body
 - /(usage.limit|quota|billing)[\s\S]{0,120}?403/i
 - /(weekly|daily|monthly|hourly)\s*(\([^)]*\))?\s*(usage\s*)?limit/i — window text capture
 - /provider chain exhausted/i — only when quota evidence also present? UT-1 says: mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted. "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses. If text has "Provider chain exhausted" AND (403 or usage-limit) → quota. If "Provider chain exhausted" alone without any quota/403/429 signals → hmm, ambiguous. Live message: "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2" appeared after 403s; the tail message alone might not include the 403s. The classifier receives the full CLI output text (developmentSummary/cliErrorMessage) — in live case the full text had the 403s. I'll treat "provider chain exhausted" + any quota-ish term (usage limit, quota) anywhere in the text → quota_exhausted; "provider chain exhausted" alone → transient? Safer: alone → null (unknown) → falls to existing behavior (reset, i.e., today's behavior). But UT-1 only requires: 403-weekly → quota; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota. Keep "exhausted"-alone → null.
- 429 / rate limit / timeout / ECONNRESET / ETIMEDOUT / "interupted" → transient (lower priority than quota).

Provider extraction:
- /([a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9.-]*[a-z0-9])?\.(?:ai|com|org|net|dev))\s+([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)\s+(?:answered|returned|responded with)\s+403/ → provider = domain
- /provider[:\s"']+([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/i fallback
- /([\w.-]+)\/[\w.-]+ answered 403/? Keep simple.

Window extraction:
- /((?:weekly|daily|monthly|hourly)(?:\s*\([^)]*\))?)\s+(?:usage\s+)?limit/i
- /(7-day|24-hour|30-day)\s+(?:usage\s+)?limit/i
Return first match text.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"

source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"

source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +

  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument

  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
